Whether a referent's answer to a collision came after the question

log_answer_stands.Rd

The log half of the answer, beside collision_answered(), which compares its value with the proposal: the newest write of distinct_username in the row's current life stands above the newest write of username carrying that proposal by the channel, the account log_channel_accounts() names. The round writes the proposal through the identity door, together with the verdict collision, the first time it finds it, so that write is the question; an answer below it was written before anybody was asked.

Usage

log_answer_stands(events, record, proposal, channel_account = NULL)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

proposal

The proposal the resolution has just made for the row.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured, for log_channel_accounts().

Value

TRUE when the answer stands.

Details

Decided on 2026-10-27, and the case is the referent who knows the convention of the suffixes and fills the field in when the row is filed, or imports it already filled, without having looked at who holds the composed name. The answer has to be written again after the proposal; REDCap logs no write that leaves a value as it was, so writing again means emptying the field and pasting the proposal anew.

Who wrote the answer is not asked here: it is an intent field, so its author is an author of the row, log_change_authors(), and the row waits for its owner when it is somebody else.

The proposal and the value in the log are folded as addresses are, on both sides. The order is REDCap's, newest first, as everywhere else in the log. A log that cannot say which account is the channel, log_channel_unknown(), holds no answer.
